annotation.kind: source-exact formalization of equations (3.3)-(3.4) and their immediately following composition in the proof of Lemma 3.1

assumptions: X and Y are real b-by-r factors and v is a real b-vector.
The two matrix-vector products are evaluated by the displayed rounded dot-product implementation in the stated order.
The standard relative floating-point model excludes overflow and underflow and has valid gamma bounds at dimensions b and r.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P15 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P15 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p15_t1_low_rank_matvec_backward_representation {b r : Nat} (fp : StandardFPModel) (X Y : P15RectMatrix b r) (v : P15Vector b) (hb : GammaValid fp.u b) (hr : GammaValid fp.u r) : let wHat := p15RoundedRectMatVec fp (p15RectTranspose Y) v; let zHat := p15RoundedRectMatVec fp X wHat; exists DeltaYT : P15RectMatrix r b, exists DeltaX : P15RectMatrix b r, p15RectFrobNorm DeltaYT <= gamma fp.u b * p15RectFrobNorm (p15RectTranspose Y) and p15RectFrobNorm DeltaX <= gamma fp.u r * p15RectFrobNorm X and wHat = p15RectMatVec (p15RectAdd (p15RectTranspose Y) DeltaYT) v and zHat = p15RectMatVec (p15RectAdd X DeltaX) wHat and zHat = p15RectMatVec (p15RectMatMul (p15RectAdd X DeltaX) (p15RectAdd (p15RectTranspose Y) DeltaYT)) v
formal_statement.plain_language: The two rounded matrix-vector products in equations (3.3)-(3.4) admit the displayed Frobenius-norm backward perturbations, and their composition is the exact perturbed low-rank action written immediately afterward.

informal_proof: Apply the standard matrix-vector backward-error result to Y^T v and then to X times the computed intermediate vector. Substitute the first exact representation into the second and reassociate the finite sums.
informal_statement: Equations (3.3)-(3.4) from the proof of Lemma 3.1, with their Frobenius-norm bounds and the exact low-rank composition written immediately afterward.
